{{Quote|Oh no! The rancor!|[[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], upon seeing the Rancor beast|<ref name="Episode 6">{{Film|VI}}</ref>}}
'''Jabba's rancor''' was a [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]] given to the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Kajidii/Legends|kajidii]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] as a birthday present from his henchmen. It was kept beneath a trapdoor in his chamber at [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|his palace]]. He was fond of dropping people into the rancor's pit and watching them be eaten.

==Biography==
===Early life===
[[File:Rancor-RotJAVA.png|thumb|left|250px|Jabba's rancor with a large bone caught in its mouth]]Native from [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]],<ref name="H2H" /> a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> a male<ref name=":1">{{SWE|characters|rancor|rancor}}</ref> rancor was being transported from the [[Tarsunt system/Legends|Tarsunt system]] by [[Grizzid]] for a [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] merchant named [[Grendu]], when it broke out, killing Grizzid and his crew, and causing the ship to crash on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name=":0">{{StoryCite|story=A Boy and His Monster: The Rancor Keeper's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>

In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' placed Kwerve's death in 0 BBY, thus indicating that the rancor was discovered around that year.</ref> A [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] [[Sandcrawler/Legends|Sandcrawler]] captain named [[Tteel Kkak]] discovered the wreckage.<ref name=":0" /> His group of [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]] informed [[Bidlo Kwerve/Legends|Bidlo Kwerve]] that a [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] ship had crashed in the Tatooinian desert, containing a fearsome creature.<ref name="SWTS:SE">''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]''</ref> Intrigued, and hoping to curry favor with Jabba, Kwerve went out to investigate along with several of Jabba's [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] guards,<ref name="db">{{DB|creature|rancor|rancor}}</ref> claiming he was going [[Womp rat/Legends|womp rat]] hunting.<ref name="wotc">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/Rancor2|series=Jabba's Rancor|text=Part 2: The Birthday Present}}</ref> In the downed ship, Bidlo Kwerve found the rancor, which was only subdued when the Corellian pirate threw eight [[Gas grenade/Legends|gas grenades]] at it.<ref name=":0" /> Both he and [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]] knew they would not be able to bring the beast back to Jabba's Palace alone and decided that working together&#x2014;something they had never done before&#x2014;was the least dangerous option.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi">''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]'', second edition</ref> The duo took the creature to the lower dungeons of the desert citadel. They presented it to Jabba as a [[Birthday/Legends|birthday]] present. Fortuna was rewarded by being made Jabba's majordomo, while Kwerve was fed to the rancor.<ref name=":0" />

===Serving Jabba===
{{Quote|I think this is a rancor. I have heard of them, but never dreamed that I would be lucky enough to see one in my lifetime.|Malakili to Bib Fortuna|<ref name=":0" />}}
[[File:Malakili_weeping.jpg|thumb|250x250px|The rancor was taken care by the human [[Malakili/Legends|Malakili]].]]
The rancor served the dual purpose of not only amusing Jabba, but also disposing of unwanted servants, musicians, or anyone else the Hutt would want to get rid of.<ref name=":1" /> With a shout of "Boska!" Jabba would activate a secret trap door in front of his throne, sending his victims to be eaten by the creature.<ref name="RotJ" /> He kept the origin of his bizzare, freakish pet a mystery.<ref>[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary|''Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary'']]</ref>

[[Malakili/Legends|Malakili]] was bought from the [[Circus Horrificus/Legends|Circus Horrificus]] in order to care for the rancor. He became very emotionally attached to it. While he took the rancor for a walk in the desert, it saved him from a small gang of [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Sand People]]. Malakili forged a close bond with the rancor, such that the creature would allow him to treat its wounds and eat meals with it.<ref name=":0" />

Despite Malakili's best cares,<ref name=":0" /> the rancor was seriuosly abused as it was forced to live in a dungeon where it could barely move and was left half-starved.<ref name="Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side" /> Jabba enjoyed pitting the rancor against other exotic monsters for his amusement. It always won, but was seriously wounded by three [[Combat arachnid/Legends|Caridan combat arachnids]]. When Malakili discovered that Jabba planned to pit the rancor against a [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragon]], which would surely kill it, he made plans to betray Jabba to [[Lady/Legends|Lady]] [[Valarian/Legends|Valarian]] and escape Tatooine with the rancor.<ref name=":0" />

At one point, the bloodthirsty gamblers demanded more violence. So Jabba ordered Malakili to train the rancor for battle, and had a special weapon harness built.<ref name=":0" /> Malakili fitted the rancor with the weapons harness and entered his master's dangerous [[Jabba's demolition games|demolition derby]].<ref name="Star Wars: Demolition">''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]''</ref> Malakili and his mount, however, did not emerge victorious in the contest.<ref>In the video game ''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]'', Malakili's winning cutscene had the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] dancer [[Lyn Me/Legends|Lyn Me]] eaten by [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|Jabba's rancor]]. However, the ''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]'' established that Lyn Me survived Jabba the Hutt, which renders the wrangler's winning cutscene non-[[canon]].</ref> Also, Jabba's [[Tusken battle talisman]] somehow ended up falling into its pit, where the rancor ate it, too.<ref name="Popup">''[[Jabba's Palace Pop-up Book]]''</ref>

In [[4 BBY/Legends|4 BBY]]<ref name="The Essential Reader's Companion">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> Jabba executed a prisoner by feeding him to his rancor, a scene witnessed by the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] dancer [[Oola/Legends|Oola]] who was terrified so much, that she forced herself onto Jabba and climb over him so she wouldn’t have to watch anymore.<ref>"[[A Time to Mourn, a Time to Dance: Oola's Tale]]" — ''[[Tales from Jabba's Palace]]''</ref>

===Death===
{{Quote|The Keepers forced Jabba's rancor into a dungeon where it could barely move. It was half-starved. Though I didn't have a choice, I'm still sorry I had to kill it.|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>}}
[[File:JubnukEaten-Chron.png|thumb|left|250px|Jabba's rancor devouring the Gamorrean guard, Jubnuk.]]
Jabba frequently used his rancor as an amusing form of execution.<ref name="RotJ" /> In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]<ref name="EAtlas" /> [[Oola/Legends|Oola]] was dropped in for resisting Jabba when she finally got fed up with his advances on her. Later, Jabba used it against [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], accidentally dropping a [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] guard named [[Jubnuk/Legends|Jubnuk]] in as well. The rancor ate Jubnuk, but Skywalker proved to be more of a challenge: the young Jedi Knight, when it first attempted to eat him, placed a large femur<ref name="RotJ" /> of a previous victim<ref name=":1" /> between its jaws, forcing the rancor to let him go before snapping it in two with effort. It tried to devour him again, but Luke smashed its hand in self-defense with a rock.<ref name="RotJ" />

Luke, out of options due to the rancor's handlers preventing him from escaping, lured it under a heavy portcullis, then smashed the control panel with a skull, causing the gate to pierce and crush the beast's skull, killing it.<ref name="RotJ" /> Ironically,<ref name="ccg">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Skull}}</ref> the skull Luke threw<ref name="RotJ" /> had belonged to its first victim, Kwerve.<ref name="ccg2">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Skull}}</ref> As it was dying, the rancor moaned weakly, with Malakili rushing to the rancor's aid and then breaking down in tears when he discovered it was too late.<ref name="RotJ" />

===Legacy===
Jubnuk was later cut out of the rancor's stomach, still alive due to both his armor and the [[Tusken battle talisman]] he found inside the stomach, which he had been tasked to find earlier.<ref name="Popup" />

Later, Luke stated that he had another reason for killing it, other than defending himself. The rancor was so abused and mistreated that rehabilitating it would have been impossible, and Luke believed that it would be best to put the poor creature out of its misery.<ref name="Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side" /> Even two decades after the fact, Luke expressed that it was a shame that he had to kill the rancor. He felt that as a species, they were such fine creatures.<ref name="Young Jedi Knights: Shadow Academy">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Shadow Academy]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I like the idea that everyone loves someone. And even the worst, most horrible monster you can imagine was loved by his keeper. And the rancor probably loved his keeper.|[[George Lucas]]|<ref name="Making">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Jabbas_Palace_dragon.jpg|250px|thumb|The creatures below Jabba's Palace]]
An image often mistaken to be the rancor battling a [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragon]] is in truth, a joke from the crew of ILM. They placed a model of one of the [[Wikipedia:Dragon|dragons]] from the film ''[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragonslayer_(1981_film) Dragonslayer]'' in the arms of the rancor model and took a picture. The picture was included in the book [[Star Wars Chronicles|''Star Wars: Chronicles'']].<ref name="Star Wars Chronicles">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref> [[Unidentified winged creature|A creature]] based on the appearance of this dragon appears in one of Jabba's creature pens in ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''.<ref name="Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref>

The rancor is a mini boss in [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition|Lord Starkiller's Mission To Tatooine]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition]]''</ref> The rancor also acted as a boss in the ''Return of the Jedi'' chapter of ''[[Star Wars Trilogy: Apprentice of the Force]]''. Although its fate was overall the same, the rancor can also "summon" more Gamorrean guards by stomping and causing more to fall down everywhere, alongside rocks. After the player backs it up to the gate, the player then delivers the coup de grace by Force-pushing a rock at the control panel.<ref name="Star Wars Trilogy: Apprentice of the Force">''[[Star Wars Trilogy: Apprentice of the Force]]''</ref>

The [[2002]] [[Infinities]] comic ''[[Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back]]'' shows Jabba possessing a pair of [[Nexu/Legends|Nexus]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] instead of the rancor,<ref>[[Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back 3|''Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back'' 3]]</ref> which he should have chronogically since [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" />

In the current ''Star Wars'' canon, the rancor was given the proper name [[Pateesa]] in [[2016]].<ref name="Life Debt">''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]''</ref>
